question: Which population, supporting reference and condition define each RAGChecker metric, and what can these diagnostic categories establish?

elements.role: Query, corpus, retrieved chunks, generated response and evaluation reference have distinct retrieval/generation/evaluation roles.
Response claims M and reference claims T are separately extracted populations, not one shared correct-claim intersection.
Reference text entails a claim; directional support rather than symmetric identity.
Chunks with at least one supported T claim versus their complement; relevant chunks can also contain misleading content.
Precision divides supported M by |M|; recall divides supported T by |T|; F1 combines them when defined.
Claim recall has T units; context precision has chunk units.
Five response-support diagnostic rates divide by |M|; utilization divides by only retrieved-supported T.

relations.type: possibly overlapping operational categories; not causal source attribution

visual_design: Original four-panel workflow and formula roles replace the source Venn geometry. Separate M/T counts and conditional denominators remain visible; full caption preserves source discrepancies, checker meaning and validation scope. No numeric model results or proportional areas drawn.
transferable_rules: Declare the counted population, support direction and conditioning for every metric. Claims, reference claims and chunks cannot share a denominator merely because they appear in the same schematic.
Do not draw overlapping diagnostic subsets as an exclusive partition, equate context faithfulness with reference correctness, or promote support categories into observed causal provenance.
gaps: Empty denominators/F1 zero cases, extraction/deduplication, executable multi-chunk checking, cross-question aggregation and experiment code revision remain unknown.
